text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- A committee of the chief justices has opposed the Pakistani government's plans to constitute special courts for speedy trials.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif gave a go-ahead to the state Privatisation Commission on Friday to put Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd on sale along with other state-run companies. He said the companies should be privatised within one year's time.
- Pakistani garment makers and exporters have asked the government to allow import of raw cotton from India.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Friday his government would not raise electricity tariff in the forthcoming budget.
- The government has embarked on a supply side economic plan because the formula of the International Monetary Fund cannot give expected results, Senate (upper house) chiarman Wasim Sajjad said.

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television on Friday that revised estimates showed Pakistan's budget deficit for fiscal 1996/97 would be at the previous year's level of 6.3 percent of GDP but should ease to five percent next year.
- Pakistan hopes to get a new medium-term loan or enhanced structural adjustment facility from the International Monetary Fund before September, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- The state-run Water and Power Development Authority has withdrawn a notice issued to Hub Power Co for termination of power purchase agreement.
NEWS
- The chief justices committee has empowered district judges to hear and dispose of case of heinous crimes.
- President Farooq Leghari leaves on Saturday for a three-day visit to the United Arab Emirates.
NATION
- Senate (upper house) witnessed an uproar on the issue of Kalabagh Dam.

- A high-level meeting attended by President Farooq Leghari, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff General Jehangir Karamat called for effective contacts with Afghanistan's Taleban movement at their meeting in Islamabad on Friday.
MUSLIM
- Opposition Pakistan People's Party staged a walkout from the National Assembly (lower house) on Friday against the behaviour of speaker Ilahi Bakhsh Soomro.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
